subject: Re: Order form — deployment boundaries, output rights, and product-use guardrails
messages:
From: Heather James <heather.james@acmehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-11-25T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: Order form redlines — IP / training / output ownership

Karthik,

Attached are Acme's redlines to the Order Form and a marked MSA excerpt. Two quick asks up front: can Redwood confirm (1) whether customer outputs (generated text/images) are treated as Customer property and excluded from any internal model retraining without an explicit opt-in, and (2) what telemetry/feedback you intend to retain for product improvement (we need specifics for procurement).

Key redline notes in the doc:
- Customer retains ownership of Customer Content and Customer Output.
- Redwood may not use Customer Content or Customer Output to train any machine learning models or adjust base models that are shared across customers.
- Limited feedback license: Customer grants right to use anonymized/aggregated telemetry for service operation and safety, not for model retraining that would produce customer-derived improvements.

We flagged a few operational questions for your team: prompt retention windows, access controls for logs, and whether there is a technical opt-out for any retention that could be used for training.

Attached: Acme_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx (redlines), MSA_redline_comments.pdf

Can you loop in legal and product and confirm a path forward before EOD Friday? Procurement requires a short summary of what Redwood can/cannot do with customer data and outputs.

Thanks,
Heather James
Sr. Procurement Manager — Acme Health

Subject: Re: Order form redlines — IP / training / output ownership

Heather — thanks for the clear redlines and the callout list. I pulled legal and product into this thread (Laura and Ben cc'd).

Short answers up front:
- Redwood's intent: Customer retains full rights to Customer Content and Customer Output. We do not, by default, use Customer Content or Customer Output to retrain public/base models.
- Feedback/telemetry: we collect operational telemetry (errors, latency, token counts) and optional customer feedback (rating flags) for service improvements. We propose a "Feedback License" limited to aggregated, de-identified metrics for service quality, safety, and stability; separate opt-in would be required for any training that incorporates customer-provided prompts/outputs.

Proposed interim language (for procurement summary):
"Customer Content" means data, prompts, and files provided by Customer. "Customer Output" means content generated by the Service in response to Customer requests. Redwood will not use Customer Content or Customer Output to train or improve base models without Customer's prior written opt-in. Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry and feedback solely to operate and improve the Service (e.g., bug fixes, throughput, safety tuning) provided such use does not recreate Customer Content or Customer Output or otherwise allow re-identification of Customer data.

Action items I propose:
1) Laura to propose specific contract language edits for the Order Form/MSA that implement the interim language above.
2) Ben to confirm operational telemetry retention windows and access controls.
3) Quick call with Acme legal tomorrow AM to walk language and confirm whether escrow or further attestations are necessary for procurement.

Heather — do these interim statements cover the procurement ask? If so I will send the redline suggestions back to you by EOD.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer

Heather / Karthik —

Thanks for the materials. Below are suggested legal edits and clarifications that map directly to Acme's commercial asks. I've included precise terms you can drop into the Order Form / MSA.

Proposed legal snippets (suggested placement: Order Form, Section "Customer Data and Use"):
1) Definitions:
- "Customer Content" means all data, text, images, audio, and other materials uploaded by or on behalf of Customer, and Customer Output.
- "Customer Output" means content generated by the Service in response to Customer requests.

2) Ownership and Use:
- Customer retains all right, title, and interest in and to Customer Content and Customer Output. Redwood shall not claim any ownership or license rights in Customer Content or Customer Output except as expressly set forth below.

3) Training and Model Use Restriction:
- Redwood will not use Customer Content or Customer Output to train, fine-tune, or improve any base or foundational models that are made available to other customers, without Customer's prior written consent.

4) Feedback License (limited):
- Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use aggregated and de-identified telemetry, usage metrics, and feedback (the "Feedback Data") solely to operate, maintain, and improve the Service for purposes including bug fixes, system performance, and safety improvements. Feedback Data shall not include Customer Content or Customer Output in any form that could reasonably be used to reconstruct or reproduce Customer Content or Customer Output.

5) Logging and Retention Controls:
- Redwood will implement reasonable retention windows (e.g., 30 days for full request/response logs, 365 days for aggregated telemetry) and role-based access controls. Specific retention windows and logging configuration are documentable in Attachment A (SOW) and configurable per customer tier.

6) Audit & Certification:
- Redwood will provide evidence of retention windows and access controls upon reasonable request (e.g., SOC 2 report, redacted logs) subject to standard confidentiality protections.

If these clauses are acceptable in principle I will prepare a redline of the Order Form and an Attachment A stub that lists default telemetry retention windows and admin controls.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

Laura / Karthik — appreciate the quick turnaround and the proposed language. A couple follow ups from procurement/legal review: 

1) Procurement needs an explicit "no-derivative-title" line that clarifies that Acme cannot be compelled to grant rights that would transfer title (i.e., no implied assignment of derivative works).
2) We need confirmation on prompt retention: the 30-day example for full request/response logs is reasonable, but is there an option for a zero-retention mode for regulated workloads (no prompt retention at all)? If not, can Redwood commit to a technical workflow for scheduled purging and a customer-controlled toggle?

Also — Acme legal asked whether Redwood will provide a signed attestation that no Customer Output was used to train models prior to go-live, and whether we can add a limited escrow or certificate-of-nontraining for the initial 12 months. Is that something Redwood can provide or we can work into the SOW?

Heather James
Sr. Procurement Manager — Acme Health
heather.james@acmehealth.com

Subject: Re: Order form redlines — IP / training / output ownership

Heather — thanks, all great questions. Confirming next steps and commitments so procurement has a short checklist they can share with budget approvers.

1) No-derivative-title: Redwood will accept and add the explicit "no-derivative-title" sentence in the Order Form: "Nothing in this Agreement transfers title in Customer Output to Redwood, and Customer will not be deemed to have assigned derivative title to Redwood by virtue of Customer's use of the Service." Laura will insert precise placement in the redline.

2) Retention / zero-retention mode: Product confirms a customer-configurable retention toggle. Default: 30 days for request/response logs (customer prompts and outputs), with an available zero-retention setting in Dedicated/Private deployments and as an add-on for Hosted via an enterprise configuration (Attachment A will record the selected setting). Ben will draft the operational checklist and timing for enabling zero-retention.

3) Attestation and initial non-training commitment: Redwood can provide a signed attestation that, for the period between contract signature and go-live, Redwood did not and will not use Customer Content or Customer Output to train base models. For the initial 12 months post-go-live, we can include a contractual covenant limiting any training use without Customer opt-in and offer a quarterly attestation on compliance (subject to confidentiality). Laura will draft the attestation language and Ben will confirm pragmatic monitoring items we can report.

Next immediate actions:
- Laura: prepare Order Form redline with the clauses agreed above and attach Attachment A (retention and access controls).
- Ben: produce a short operational appendix (Attachment A) that lists retention toggles, purging workflow, and admin roles.
- Karthik: I will schedule a 30-minute legal + procurement sync for tomorrow morning (proposed 9:30 AM PT) and share a one-page procurement summary for Acme's finance team.

If that plan sounds good I will send the redlines and the procurement summary to Heather by EOD tomorrow. Also looping in our CS and Security teams for any follow-up evidence requests.

Thanks — talk soon.

Karthik Iyer
